nodes.label: piSignage Log Download Path Traversal (Arbitrary File Read)
nodes.precondition: Attacker possesses network connectivity to the piSignage player API (versions prior to 2.6.4) and low-privilege authenticated user credentials.
nodes.postcondition: Attacker downloads arbitrary system files via 'api/settings/log?file=../' directory traversal, exfiltrating sensitive configurations, password hashes, and system credentials from the Raspberry Pi.

nodes.label: Raspberry Pi Credential and Configuration Extraction
nodes.precondition: Attacker downloads arbitrary system files via 'api/settings/log?file=../' directory traversal, exfiltrating sensitive configurations, password hashes, and system credentials from the Raspberry Pi.
nodes.postcondition: Attacker recovers authentication credentials for web administrative components (e.g., RaspAP) and identifies unhardened default OS account settings.

nodes.label: RaspAP Misconfigured Web Console Command Execution
nodes.precondition: Attacker possesses authenticated access to RaspAP 2.5 web interface containing misconfigured 'includes/webconsole.php'.
nodes.postcondition: Attacker executes arbitrary OS commands and uploads files onto the underlying Raspberry Pi operating system as the web server user.

nodes.label: Raspberry Pi OS Default Account Privilege Escalation
nodes.precondition: Attacker has local shell access or interactive service access on Raspberry Pi OS through version 5.10 where the default password 'raspberry' for account 'pi' has not been changed.
nodes.postcondition: Attacker escalates privileges to root/administrator on the Raspberry Pi host via sudo with default credentials.

nodes.label: Malicious Acoustic Signal Generation on Raspberry Pi
nodes.precondition: Attacker escalates privileges to root/administrator on the Raspberry Pi host via sudo with default credentials, gaining control over audio output to speakers powered by the Raspberry Pi 3 B+ or 4 B.
nodes.postcondition: Attacker triggers playback of targeted audio/speech through speakers, causing the sound-induced load to modulate the Raspberry Pi power line and power indicator LED intensity.

nodes.label: Glowworm Optical Side-Channel Acoustic Recovery
nodes.precondition: Raspberry Pi 3 B+ or 4 B device (through 2021-08-09) supplies power directly to audio-output equipment (speakers) whose playback modulates power consumption and power LED intensity; attacker has optical line-of-sight equipped with a telescope and an electro-optical sensor.
nodes.postcondition: Attacker analyzes measurements from the electro-optical sensor directed at the power indicator LED, successfully reconstructing and recovering the speech signals played through the speakers.

nodes.label: Oculus Browser UI Injection and Code Execution
nodes.precondition: Victim navigates to an attacker-controlled remote web page using Oculus Browser (versions 5.2.7 through 5.7.11).
nodes.postcondition: Attacker injects arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, successfully spoofing user interface elements and executing arbitrary code in an unprivileged local user context.

nodes.label: Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe Hardlink Privileged File Write LPE
nodes.precondition: Attacker has local unprivileged access on a Windows system running Oculus Desktop prior to version 1.44.0.32849 where privileged process OVRRedir.exe writes to an unprivileged log file.
nodes.postcondition: Attacker establishes a hard link to the target log file, causing OVRRedir.exe to write to arbitrary files and elevating privileges to SYSTEM.

nodes.label: Oculus Desktop OVRServiceLauncher Handle Leak LPE
nodes.precondition: Attacker has local unprivileged process execution on a Windows host running Oculus Desktop (versions after 1.39 and prior to 31.1.0.67.507) affected by OVRServiceLauncher.exe handle mismanagement.
nodes.postcondition: Attacker acquires an exposed privileged process handle via the unprivileged process, escalating privileges to SYSTEM.

nodes.label: Physical PCI Interface Access on NVIDIA Jetson
nodes.precondition: Unprivileged attacker obtains physical access to an NVIDIA Jetson board running a vulnerable Jetson Linux distribution.
nodes.postcondition: Attacker interfaces a physical device directly to the PCI bus of the NVIDIA Jetson board.

nodes.label: NVIDIA Jetson Linux IOMMU Misconfiguration Memory Compromise
nodes.precondition: Attacker interfaces a physical device directly to the PCI bus of the NVIDIA Jetson board where an IOMMU configuration error exists in NVIDIA Jetson Linux.
nodes.postcondition: Attacker achieves direct read/write DMA access to the entire system address space through the PCI bus, causing code execution, local privilege escalation, Denial of Service, and compromise of system-wide data integrity and confidentiality extending to other components.

edges.label: Exploiting path traversal in api/settings/log yields arbitrary file access, allowing attacker to harvest web console and OS credentials
Harvested credentials provide authenticated access to RaspAP 2.5 web interface
Harvested OS configuration confirms unchanged default account 'pi' with password 'raspberry'
OS command execution via includes/webconsole.php enables interactive shell access to invoke sudo using default credentials
Full root permissions allow attacker to manipulate hardware sound output and execute audio routines on the Raspberry Pi
Sound played through Raspberry Pi-powered speakers modulates power line draw and LED luminescence, exposing speech signals to remote optical sensors
Local unprivileged code execution from browser exploitation provides the local access required to create log hard links for OVRRedir.exe
Local unprivileged process execution spawned from browser exploitation interacts with OVRServiceLauncher.exe to capture leaked privileged handles
Physical PCI bus connection enables hardware-level direct memory operations that exploit the IOMMU misconfiguration in Jetson Linux
